info.title: Drift API
info.description: drift's versioned API: environment reads, the full environment lifecycle, and promotion to rc and to production. Authenticate with a CLI bearer credential or a browser session cookie; when both are presented the bearer wins and a bearer that fails to verify is a 401, never a fallback. Every operation enforces a role floor server-side — `read-only` for reads, `preview` for every environment mutation, `release` for a promotion — so a read-only credential cannot reach a write and a preview credential cannot promote. Production promotion requires MORE than a role: the credential must also carry the `promote:prd` scope, which only a 15-minute credential minted through an interactive browser sign-in has. A `release` credential — or an `admin` one — without that scope is refused with 403 and `data.type` `urn:drift:problem:elevation-required`, which is the signal to elevate rather than to give up; the refusal also carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. Requests are rate limited per credential (per signed-in user for cookie callers); a 429 carries `Retry-After` in whole seconds and is not avoidable by changing any request header. Errors share one envelope: `{ defined, code, status, message, data }`, where `data.type` is a `urn:drift:problem:` identifier; a 409 whose type is `urn:drift:problem:invalid-transition` additionally carries `data.state` and `data.event`, the state the entity was in and the lifecycle event that was refused. Mutations accept work and return an id; poll `GET /environments/{ref}` or `GET /releases/promotions/active` for the outcome.

bearerAuth.description: A drift CLI credential: `Authorization: Bearer drift_<token>`. Minted from the drift credentials page, shown once, hashed at rest, and revocable with effect from the next request. Its authority is the LOWER of the role snapshot taken at mint and the owner's role at the time of the request, so a later demotion narrows it and a later promotion does not widen it; a banned owner's credential is refused outright. Takes precedence over `cookieAuth` when both are present.

cookieAuth.name: better-auth.session_token
cookieAuth.description: Better Auth session cookie, set by the browser sign-in flow. The name VARIES with the deployment: a production deployment sets secure cookies and the same credential arrives as `__Secure-better-auth.session_token`, while a plain-HTTP one (a `kubectl port-forward`, local development) sets `better-auth.session_token`. An `apiKey` scheme has one name and cannot express the alternative, so this declares the unprefixed spelling and the prefixed one is named here — send whichever the sign-in flow set, and prefer `bearerAuth` for a non-browser client.

get.description: Reports the caller's own email, effective role, and — for a bearer credential — its label and expiry. Takes no parameters and can only describe the credential presented on the request; there is no way to ask about another principal or to list the credentials one holds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.description: Environments newest first. Pass `status` one or more times to narrow to a status set; omit it for every environment including terminal ones. Pass `creator` to narrow to environments created by that email (exact match).

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Dispatches builds and returns immediately with the new environment's id; poll `GET /environments/{ref}` for progress. At least one repository must be on a non-default branch — staging already runs every repository on its default branch. Rejected with 409 if the slug is held by a live environment or its namespace is still tearing down.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.summary: Get an environment by id or slug
get.description: `ref` is either the environment's UUID or its slug. Slug lookup resolves only environments that are neither `destroyed` nor `canceled`, so a slug that has been reused over time addresses the one live environment holding it; address a torn-down environment by id.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.description: Returns only the environment's current status. `ref` is either the environment's UUID or its slug. Designed as a lightweight poll target: one query, no services or builds, so polling every 30 seconds costs a fraction of what `GET /environments/{ref}` would.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.summary: Get database access parameters for an environment
get.description: Returns the database-connection parameters the CLI needs for `drift env tunnel` and `drift env db`. `ref` is either the environment's UUID or its slug. When the Install does not publish ephemeral database access (or the lower tier is credentials-shaped), the response carries `published: false` — absence, not an error.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

delete.description: Fires destroy intent and returns; teardown is driven to completion by drift's destroy-cleanup cron, so the environment stays `destroying` for some minutes before it reaches `destroyed`. A second call while it is already tearing down is a 409.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Only valid while the environment is building or has failed to build. Cancelling does not tear anything down — destroy the environment to release its namespace.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Clones a `destroyed` or `canceled` environment's repositories, branches, TTL and visibility into a NEW environment and dispatches its builds. `environmentId` addresses the SOURCE; the response carries the id of the environment that was created. Rejected with 409 if the slug is back in use.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Scales every workload to zero and hibernates the CNPG database, keeping the volumes. Only valid from `running`. The TTL is frozen while asleep and resumes on wake.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Two-phase: the data tier comes up first, then the applications. The environment reports `waking` until ArgoCD sees phase 2 healthy. The TTL is extended by however long it slept.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Adds hours to the expiry. Bounded per request and cumulatively: a request that would carry the total past drift's ceiling is rejected with 400 and nothing is changed. NOT idempotent — two calls extend twice.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

put.description: Moves the environment between the internal and public ALB groups and re-commits its gitops manifest. Setting the visibility it already has is a 409, so this is safe to retry but not to use as an assertion.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Add a service to an environment
post.description: Wires a repository into the environment on the given branch, dispatches its build and re-commits the manifest. Every dependency of the repository must already be present. Adding one that is already there is a 409.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

delete.summary: Remove a service from an environment
delete.description: Deletes the service, cancels its in-flight builds and re-commits the manifest. The last remaining service cannot be removed, and a sleeping environment must be woken first.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

put.description: Repoints the service at another branch, cancels its in-flight builds and dispatches a new one. The environment returns to `building`.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Re-dispatches the service's build. Only valid when the service has no build on its current branch, or its latest build on that branch is failed or canceled. For a monorepo every retryable sibling service on the same branch is retried together; siblings on other branches are not.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Re-resolves repo configs, preflights images, and re-commits the gitops manifest. Only valid from deploy_failed with infrastructure ready.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Triggers an e2e test run against the environment. Only valid when the environment is running with infrastructure ready. Returns 409 if a run is already in progress. Returns 502 if the workflow dispatch fails.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.description: Returns one e2e test run for an environment. Returns 404 when the run does not exist or belongs to a different environment. Runs outlive their environment, so a run of a destroyed environment is still readable by that environment's id.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.summary: Get stg and rc release state
get.description: Promoted image tags and commit SHAs read from gitops, joined with live pod health from Kubernetes. A failure on either side degrades to an `error` string on the affected namespace rather than failing the request.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.summary: Get the in-flight promotion and recent history

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.
Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Fails a promotion that is stuck — the retag workflow was cancelled, the target was rolled back by hand, no ArgoCD notification ever arrived. Only valid while the promotion is `dispatched`, `promoting` or `deploying`; one that has already reached a terminal state is refused with 409 naming that state. The promotion moves to the failure state the lifecycle machine allows from where it stood (`deploy_failed` from `deploying`, `failed` from the two earlier states) — there is no separate `cancelled` state, and the response names both statuses so a caller does not have to derive the target. The operator's `reason`, when given, is recorded on the promotion and in its `promotion.canceled` audit row.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Promote services from stg to rc
post.description: Retags each named service's current stg image as rc and dispatches the retag workflow, grouped by repository so a monorepo is dispatched once. Returns immediately with the promotion's id; poll `GET /releases/promotions/active` for progress. Rejected with 409 while an rc promotion is already in flight, or when the services selected from one repository sit at different stg commits, and with 404 if a service is not registered or is absent from the stg namespace.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Dispatch a hotfix build to rc
post.description: Resolves the named branch's HEAD in each service's repository and dispatches that repository's hotfix workflow against it, tagging the result `rc-<sha>`. For emergencies: the build does not pass through stg. The target is the path, not a parameter — a hotfix to production is a production promotion and is not on this surface.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Promote services from rc to production
post.description: Retags each named service's current rc image as prd and dispatches the production workflow, grouped by repository so a monorepo is dispatched once. REQUIRES AN ELEVATED CREDENTIAL: a `release` credential alone is refused with 403 `urn:drift:problem:elevation-required`; mint a 15-minute elevated credential scoped to `promote:prd` on your Drift Install's /credentials page (an interactive browser sign-in is required), then run the promotion once with `DRIFT_TOKEN` set to it (e.g. `DRIFT_TOKEN=drift_... drift release promote prd ...`) — this leaves your stored credential untouched. Returns immediately with the promotion's id; poll `GET /releases/promotions/active` for progress. Rejected with 409 while a production promotion is already in flight, or when the services selected from one repository sit at different rc commits, and with 404 if a service is not registered or is absent from the rc namespace.

WWW-Authenticate.description: RFC 6750 challenge, present when the refusal is a missing scope rather than an insufficient role: `Bearer realm="drift", error="insufficient_scope", scope="promote:prd"`. Absent on a plain role refusal.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Dispatch a hotfix build to production
post.description: Resolves the named branch's HEAD in each service's repository and dispatches that repository's hotfix workflow against it, deploying to production without passing through stg or rc. REQUIRES AN ELEVATED CREDENTIAL scoped to `promote:prd`; a `release` credential is refused with 403 `urn:drift:problem:elevation-required`; mint a 15-minute elevated credential on your Drift Install's /credentials page and run the promotion once with `DRIFT_TOKEN` set to it (e.g. `DRIFT_TOKEN=drift_... drift release promote prd hotfix ... --branch ...`) — this leaves your stored credential untouched. The target is the path, not a parameter: a body field naming `rc` or `prd` is ignored, because the route selects the operation and the operation selects what it requires.

WWW-Authenticate.description: RFC 6750 challenge, present when the refusal is a missing scope rather than an insufficient role: `Bearer realm="drift", error="insufficient_scope", scope="promote:prd"`. Absent on a plain role refusal.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.description: Every repository drift knows about, including inactive ones, with the per-customer application group each belongs to.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.description: Branches with a commit in the last month, sorted by name. `q` filters by substring.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.description: The queue as the QA page's sections: In testing, Re-check (a Linked PR head moved since its approval), Ready for QA (oldest entry first), Upcoming, Decided (14 days, approvals and exemptions; collapsed in the UI) and — for an approver — the carry-over candidates. Each card carries its Linked PRs, the `drift/qa` state per head, its open session and the failed tracker writes with the ids Retry needs.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.summary: Get one QA ticket in full
get.description: One card in full: every session with its event timeline, every approval, rejection and exemption with who, when and why, and the tracker writes with their state and last error. Takes a Ticket key only, matched case-insensitively (tracker keys are uppercase); a sub-task's key resolves to no Ticket — use its parent's key.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

get.summary: Get QA sync, outbox and evaluation health
get.description: Each sync phase's cursor, last success and last error; the tracker outbox backlog by state; the evaluation-due markers past the alert threshold; and the tracker's reachability as the last sync recorded it. Never calls the tracker.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Partitions the Ticket's open Linked PRs so no partition holds two PRs of one Repository; omit `prs` for the first partition with no open session. A rebuild of a developer's environment happens under them — the card warns before confirming.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Clears `unacknowledgedChange` for the session's owner, `qa` or an admin without approving. A session that is not `open` is a 409.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Ends the session without a verdict, so the Ticket's `drift/qa` pending text goes away. A session that is already `ended` is a 409.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Refused unless the session is open, the environment is `running` and the shown generation is the verified one that runs the covered PRs' heads. `retested` or a `no-retest` reason is required when the session saw a change. Files are base64 in `files`.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Records a rejection on the covered PRs, revokes approvals on those same (PR, sha) pairs — including a sibling Ticket's — bumps the affected Tickets' verdict epochs and moves them to the rejected status. The comment is required; files are base64 in `files`.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Queues a tracker comment (and its attachments) for the Ticket. No session and no evaluator: this is QA saying something, not a verdict.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Queues the move back to the project's queue status. Refused as a 409 when drift's last-synced view already has the Ticket in the queue, approved or Done — retry after the next sync.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: `scope: "pr"` needs `pullRequestId` and exempts that PR across pushes; `scope: "ticket"` needs `ticketKey` and covers the PRs linked at that moment. Either way the reason is required and the completion evaluator runs.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.description: Revokes the exemption. A Ticket-scope exemption additionally revokes every approval of its Ticket, bumps the epoch and moves an approved Ticket back to the queue; a PR-scope one leaves the Ticket's approvals alone.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Revoke a QA approval or exemption
post.description: Name exactly one of `approvalId` or `exemptionId`. A revocation bumps the Ticket's verdict epoch and re-runs the completion evaluator.

413.description: The request body exceeds the mount's 10 MB limit, read from its declared Content-Length or measured for a chunked body.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always present on a 429.

post.summary: Link a pull request to a QA ticket
post.description: Creates a manual link (or reactivates a removed one). A PR already linked to the Ticket is a 409.

post.description: Removes the link and recomputes the gate for the PR's head. A pair that is not linked is a 404.

post.summary: Carry a ticket's pull requests over
post.description: Only for a Ticket the tracker already approved without a drift completion: records its open Linked PRs at their current heads. Carry-overs are sha-bound and never revoked. A Ticket not awaiting completion is a 400.

post.description: Re-queues a `failed` write — `claimed` when an earlier attempt may have landed, else `pending`. Any other state is a 409.
